name: Self-Refine
institution: Carnegie Mellon University (CMU) / Allen Institute for AI (AllenAI); collaborators from University of Washington, NVIDIA, UC San Diego, Google Research
what_evolved: Context记忆与提示 (context/prompt at inference time). No model weights or architecture are changed; a single LLM is reused as generator, critic, and refiner via prompt-only iteration.
skill_as_artifact: 否. The refinement (feedback + improved output) is ephemeral and consumed within a single task run; no reusable skill artifact is persisted across tasks or sessions.
skill_encoding: 自然语言 (natural-language feedback and refined outputs). Feedback is actionable text covering problem localization + improvement instruction.
skill_granularity: 策略规则/见解 (insight-level actionable feedback). Multi-aspect, localized critique guiding localized edits rather than atomic actions or full workflows.
how_method: rollout_optimization (text-space, non-gradient) combined with reward-based self-feedback. FEEDBACK -> REFINE loop: same LLM generates an internal textual reward (critique), then re-decodes the output conditioned on that feedback, iterating until a stopping criterion. No SFT, no RL, no extra weights.
learning_signal_source: 自我反思 / LLM-as-judge (self). The same LLM that produced the output also critiques it; no external human or environment feedback required.
reward_granularity: process. Feedback pinpoints specific aspects/locations and gives concrete improvement instructions, not just a scalar outcome score.
learning_paradigm: online; on-policy. Generation, critique, and refinement all happen at test time using the model's own outputs (no offline data, no off-policy corpus).
when_evolve: intra-test-time. The feedback-refine loop runs online during a single task inference; nothing is learned/trained between tasks.
trigger: 事件触发 (event-triggered on initial output generation). The loop starts after the initial output y0 and repeats until is_refinement_sufficient (stopping criterion) is met or a max-iteration cap is reached.
library_structure: 无持久技能库 (none). Only intra-task history is kept by appending prior outputs to the prompt; no cross-task or persistent library/vector store/graph.
retrieval_method: 无检索 (none / in-context history only). Past iterations are appended to the running prompt rather than retrieved from a store; no semantic/keyword retrieval is used.
validation: LLM-judge (self-feedback acts as validator) + validation gating (is_refinement_sufficient stopping function). External evaluation uses human preference and task-specific automatic metrics.
error_correction: 自我修订 (self-revision). The REFINE module rewrites the output guided by actionable feedback; bounded to a finite number of iterations to avoid endless loops.
test_env: 通用 (general). 7 diverse benchmark tasks: dialogue response generation, code optimization, math reasoning (GSM), acronym generation, story generation, sentiment reversal/review rewriting, toxicity removal, commonsense/constrained generation.
where_deploy: general (general-purpose text generation/refinement; not specialized to a single vertical).
metrics: Human preference rate (paired human evaluation) and task-specific automatic metrics (e.g., pass@k for code, accuracy for math, BLEU/ROUGE/BERTScore for dialogue & rewriting, concept coverage, acronym scores). Iterative improvement rate per iteration also reported.
key_results: Across all 7 tasks, Self-Refine outputs were preferred over same-LLM one-step generation by both humans and automatic metrics, improving ~20% absolute on average; gains range from ~5% to >40%. Even GPT-4 improves at test time. Improvement is iterative and observable per iteration; no supervised data, RL, or extra training needed.
limitations: 1) transferability/capability dependence: effectiveness relies on the model's own self-reflection ability; weaker models (e.g., GPT-3.5) often give poor or misleading feedback. 2) Diminishing / negative returns after a few iterations (over-refinement can degrade output). 3) scalability/cost: multiple extra LLM calls per task increase latency and token cost. 4) No persistent learning: no skill library, no cross-task memory, so gains do not accumulate. 5) controllability/eval-hacking risk: incorrect self-feedback can steer the refinement toward worse outputs.
